annotations.title: minFoldLevel via Nat.find
annotations.body: The minimum fold level is defined classically via Nat.find on the predicate 'k ≥ 1 ∧ IsKFoldConstructible d k'. Existence is guaranteed by the algebraic completeness theorem from OQ-02.

annotations.title: Multiplicativity is the key structural theorem
annotations.body: constructible_mul_iff shows that k-fold constructibility is 'multiplicative' in the sense that a product m·n is k-fold constructible iff both factors are. This directly implies minFoldLevel(m·n) = max(minFoldLevel m, minFoldLevel n).

annotations.title: Nat.find_min and Nat.find_min' for minimality
annotations.body: Two dual facts: Nat.find_min gives that no smaller k works (minimality), while Nat.find_min' gives that the minimum is ≤ any valid k (upper bound). Together they yield the complete characterization minFoldLevel d ≤ k ↔ d is k-fold constructible.

annotations.title: Prime fold levels are exact
annotations.body: For the j-th prime p_j (0-indexed), minFoldLevel(p_j) = j. This is the sharpest possible statement: p_j needs exactly j folds, not j-1 (too large for p_{j-1}-smooth) and not j+1 (already j-fold constructible).

annotations.title: minFoldLevel 42 = 3: the dominant prime controls
annotations.body: 42 = 2·3·7. The factor 7 (the 3rd prime) is the dominant one: minFoldLevel 42 = max(minFoldLevel 2, minFoldLevel 3, minFoldLevel 7) = max(1, 1, 3) = 3. Three simultaneous folds are both necessary and sufficient.
